Nobody cooks them that fastHow to make it500ml milk500ml water1 tsp salt150g stone-ground grits or polenta40g butter80g sharp cheddar, gratedBring the milk, water and salt to the boil.Whisk in the grits, then stir over low heat until creamy. It takes much longer than five minutes.Finish with the butter and cheddar.Fried green tomatoesCornmeal crust, remouladeAlabama's finestHow to make it3 green tomatoes1 tsp salt150ml buttermilk120g fine cornmealsalt and pepper, to taste (for the cornmeal)250ml neutral oil, for frying100g mayonnaise1 tsp mustard1 tbsp capers, choppedhot sauce, a dashSlice the tomatoes 1cm thick, salt and leave for 10 minutes, then pat dry.Dip in buttermilk, then in the cornmeal seasoned with salt and pepper.Shallow-fry in the oil at 180°C for 2 minutes a side in batches.Mix the mayonnaise, mustard, capers and hot sauce for the remoulade.Biscuits & gravyTwo biscuits, sausage gravyWhere Vinny tries to order breakfastHow to make it300g self-raising flour, for the biscuits2 tbsp self-raising flour, extra for the gravy80g butter, frozen200ml buttermilk400g pork sausages500ml full cream milksalt, to tasteblack pepper, to tasteHeat the oven to 220°C. Grate the frozen butter into the 300g self-raising flour with a pinch of salt and toss to coat.Stir in the buttermilk to make a soft dough, fold it over on itself three times, pat out 2cm thick and cut 8 biscuits.Bake the biscuits on a lined tray until risen and golden.Squeeze the sausage meat out of the skins and brown it in a frying pan, breaking it up as it cooks.Stir in the extra flour for a minute, then add the milk a little at a time and simmer until thick, with plenty of black pepper. Split the biscuits and spoon the gravy over.MainsChicken fried steakCream gravy, mashed potatoesSac-O-Suds, the corner store where the whole mess startedHow to make it600g minute steaks (4)150g plain flour, seasoned, for the coating200ml buttermilk250ml neutral oil, for frying2 tbsp plain flour, for the gravy400ml milk1 tsp black pepper800g mashed potatoFor the mash: boil 920g peeled floury potatoes until soft, drain well and mash with the butter and milk.Pound the steaks very thin.Dredge in seasoned flour, dip in buttermilk, then flour again.Shallow-fry 3 minutes a side until crisp.Pour off most of the oil, stir the gravy flour into the pan, whisk in the milk and simmer thick with lots of black pepper.Serve over the mashed potato.SweetsBlackberry cobblerWarm, with pouring creamMona Lisa's pick. Wazoo, Alabama, ticking clock and allHow to make it750g blackberries100g sugar, for the filling1 tbsp cornflour80g butter, cold200g self-raising flour50g sugar, for the topping150ml milk300ml creamToss the blackberries with the sugar and cornflour in a dish.Rub the butter into the flour and the topping sugar, add the milk and drop spoonfuls on top.Bake at 190°C for 35 minutes.Serve with cream.DrinksWazoo peach sweet teaBy the pitcher, lemon on the sideSo sweet your teeth hurtHow to make it2 ripe peaches, sliced, plus 1 for serving120g caster sugar150ml water6 black tea bags1 L boiling water1/2 lemon, juiced1 sprig mint per glass1 bag iceSimmer the peaches with the sugar and water for 10 minutes, mash lightly and strain, keeping the syrup.Steep the tea bags in the boiling water for 5 minutes and remove.Stir in the peach syrup and lemon juice and chill for 2 hours.Serve over ice with fresh peach slices and mint.
